title: Peak-Load Call Service for Mid-Size Factories
one_liner: Predict the handful of hours a year that set a facility's capacity charge and alert the plant manager to cut load, paid as a share of verified savings.
customer: Commercial and industrial sites of 300 kW to 5 MW in PJM (and ERCOT 4CP) territories that demand-response aggregators ignore: cold storage, water and wastewater plants, plastics and aggregates producers, ice rinks and indoor farms. Energy brokers and consultants are the channel.
problem: A customer's capacity tag (PLC) is set by usage during a few system-peak hours, and its cost then sits on every bill for a year. PJM capacity prices have risen roughly tenfold since 2024/25, with recent auctions clearing at the cap of about $330/MW-day, so a 1 MW site's tag is worth six figures. Owners either never curtail and overpay, or curtail on 20+ hot days and lose production. Aggregators skim 20 to 40% and focus on large accounts.
solution: Model the probability that each upcoming hour ranks in the system's top peaks for the site's zone or utility rules. Use weather ensembles, load forecasts, calendar effects and, critically, the season's running maximum so far. Send a text or BMS signal with the expected value of curtailing against the plant's own curtailment cost. Cut curtailment days from about 25 to about 8 and stop alerting once the peaks have been 'caught'.
why_now: Data-center load growth has pushed PJM capacity clearing prices to the cap two auctions in a row, and those costs are now hitting commercial bills. Open AI weather ensembles (ECMWF AIFS, NOAA) make sharper probabilistic forecasts cheap. The just-finished 2026 summer is fresh evidence for a backtest pitch.
revenue_model: 20 to 25% of verified savings (measured from the next year's PLC change), a $250 to $500 monthly alert subscription, and $2K to $5K paid load audits. Brokers and consultants get a channel rebate.
non_obvious_insight: Quants see 'top 5 hours out of 4,000' as an order-statistics and optimal-stopping problem with asymmetric payoffs, not a pure forecasting problem. As the season's record load rises, the threshold to enter the top 5 becomes known, the option value of alerts collapses, and you can stop curtailing early. Incumbents earn more the more events they call, so their models over-alert. The savings show up a year later on an invoice nobody links to behavior, so customers underinvest without a counterfactual 'what your tag would have been' report.
first_30_days: Use the off-season to pull public PJM hourly load and zonal data, backtest 2019 to 2026 peaks, and generate a free 'what your tag would have been' report for 100 facilities found through EIA and utility-tariff lists. Sell $3K load audits to the first five, sign shared-savings pilots for summer 2027, and recruit two energy brokers as channel partners.

title: Human Baseline Vault for AI Detection
one_liner: Proctored, ID-verified, unassisted human writing and speech, timestamped and sealed, sold first as ground truth for detector calibration and later as low-background evaluation data.
customer: AI-detection vendors, ed-tech firms and publishers, university integrity offices, trust-and-safety teams, and AI labs' evaluation teams.
problem: Studies report detector false-positive rates of 5-20% on native English and up to 61% on non-native writing. 25+ universities have restricted detectors, and a February 2026 New York court ordered Adelphi to expunge a student's AI accusation. Vendors cannot prove error rates by population because clean post-2022 human ground truth is unknowable, since everyone's 'human' data may be AI-assisted.
solution: Recruit 20k+ verified people across strata (non-native English, neurodivergent, technical, legal and academic writers, age bands) to write and speak in proctored sessions. Samples are timestamped and hash-anchored. Sell calibration sets and per-population false-positive certificates to detector vendors, then an annually refreshed vault as 'low-background steel' for evaluations and future disputes.
why_now: Over half of web traffic is automated and training and evaluation sets are increasingly contaminated. Lawsuits and university bans mean detector buyers now need error rates by population, and AI labs need uncontaminated human evaluation data.
revenue_model: $50-250k dataset licences, $20-75k per detector audit and certificate, and annual refresh subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Like pre-1945 steel free of nuclear fallout, verified pre-contamination human data gets more valuable every year, and its value lies in the chain of custody, not the text itself.
first_30_days: Recruit 500 participants through two university partners for a native versus non-native pilot. Pitch two detector vendors and one ed-tech firm. Publish an independent study on false positives by population to earn press.

title: Business Identity Watch: LifeLock for LLCs
one_liner: Continuous monitoring of the state filings, liens and listings that define a small business, with a fast response kit when someone hijacks them.
customer: Owners of LLCs and sole proprietorships, reached through community banks, insurance agents, CPAs and registered-agent companies.
problem: Formation is cheap and online, and US domestic companies no longer file beneficial-ownership reports (FinCEN's final rule, August 2026). Census restated its formation series and excluded internet-sales-linked applications from some series, which suggests formation counts are polluted by non-real businesses (inference). Fraudsters can file fake officer or agent changes, register lookalike LLCs and domains, hijack listings and file bogus liens. Owners find out when a collections letter arrives.
solution: Monitor Secretary of State filings across states with open bulk feeds, UCC indexes, lookalike entity names and domains, and Google Business Profile edits. Alert the owner and provide pre-drafted correction filings, fraud affidavits, a registered-agent switch, and a bank notification letter.
why_now: There is no federal ownership registry to lean on, formation is cheap, and AI makes synthetic-identity and lookalike-business fraud cheaper to run.
revenue_model: $9-19 per entity per month, a $299 incident-response fee, and bulk banking deals at about $2 per entity per month.
non_obvious_insight: The state filing is the root of trust for a small business, and nobody watches it. Identity-theft companies watch people, not entities, and a bank that already knows the business is the natural distributor.
first_30_days: Pick five states with open bulk filing data and build change alerts. Pilot with 200 LLCs through one community bank or bookkeeper. Track fraud events detected and time to resolve.

title: SpaceX Exposure Verification Desk for Advisors
angle: Pairing 2: Space economy x Cybersecurity/identity fraud (retail scams and deepfakes)
one_liner: A due-diligence service that tells advisors and retail investors whether a 'SpaceX exposure' SPV actually holds anything, and flags impersonation and deepfake endorsements timed to launch and IPO news.
customer: Registered investment advisers, family offices, broker-dealer compliance teams and private-bank due-diligence desks being pitched SPVs and notes marketed as SpaceX or Starlink exposure. Secondary: sophisticated retail via a subscription.
problem: Demand for SpaceX exposure is intense (Starlink about 12M subscribers, $11.4B 2025 revenue, Starship reached orbit on 28 Sept 2026), but shares are transfer-restricted, so anything offered is indirect: SPVs of SPVs with stacked fees, sold over LinkedIn, WhatsApp and Telegram, some holding nothing. Deepfake Musk endorsements and fake launch livestreams add a scam layer. Lumpy events such as the 16 Sept 2026 Valor distribution add confusion about what is real.
solution: (1) Map every SPV using SpaceX or Starlink naming from SEC Form D and adviser filings, with sponsor history, fee stacks and upstream fund lineage. (2) Holdings attestation by obtaining custodian, transfer agent or upstream-fund confirmation. (3) Compare marketing claims against issuer transfer restrictions and last known tender pricing. (4) A red-flag score (offshore layers, unlicensed sellers, cloned domains) and an alert feed on new offerings and impersonation around launch days and any listing.
why_now: IPO speculation, the Valor stock distribution on 16 Sept 2026, Starship's orbital flight and a record Golden Dome and launch boom are all feeding retail FOMO. Scam economics are inverting (tools cost about $50 while average payments rose 253%) and AI deepfakes are cheap. If a listing happens, the desk pivots to lock-up and SPV-unwind verification, so it does not depend on one date.
revenue_model: $750-2,500 per SPV verification report, $499 per month for adviser subscriptions with alerts, and enterprise seats for compliance teams. Later expansion to other hot pre-IPO space names.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing is not access to SpaceX but the truth about what an SPV holds. The key facts (Form D filings, fee layers, issuer restrictions) are public and cheap to analyze, yet every hype cycle mints exposure products faster than compliance staff can diligence. Buyers pay for a signed opinion that gives them cover to say no.
first_30_days: Scrape EDGAR for SpaceX and Starlink SPV names and publish an 'SPV Layer Map' with fee stacks. Send it to 200 RIAs and compliance officers. Offer 3 free verifications, then sell the next ones at $1,500. Set up domain-impersonation monitoring keyed to launch dates. Position as research and diligence, not investment advice.

title: Pickleball Noise Measurement Standard and Monitoring
one_liner: A court-defensible protocol, sensor kit and certification for measuring pickleball noise, sold to towns, HOAs and clubs.
customer: Parks and planning departments, HOAs, private clubs, court builders and municipal attorneys.
problem: Paddle impacts read roughly 70-80 dBA at 15 ft against 40-55 dBA ambient, and disputes are closing or limiting courts. In April 2026 a Missouri judge voided Kirkwood's restrictions as 'arbitrary, capricious and invalid' because noise could not be consistently measured. That leaves cities, clubs and neighbors all without an enforceable standard.
solution: A measurement protocol for impulsive, tonal sports noise (peak and Leq metrics, distance and background correction), a calibrated ~$500 sensor kit with cloud reporting and automatic compliance reports, expert-witness-ready PDFs, and an 'approved low-impact site' certification that helps at permit hearings. Add mitigation advice (barriers, quiet paddles and balls).
why_now: The Kirkwood ruling and hundreds of local ordinance fights, with participation at 24.3M and rising.
revenue_model: Kit sale or rental ($500 plus $30/month monitoring), $2-5k per-site certification, $1.5k expert reports, and protocol licensing to municipalities.
non_obvious_insight: Noise fights are fights over measurement. Whoever supplies the trusted protocol becomes the referee both sides must use, and courts have already said unmeasurable ordinances fail.
first_30_days: Contact 10 town attorneys and HOA boards currently in noise disputes and offer loaner sensor rigs. Publish an open draft protocol with an acoustical-engineer advisor. Aim for the first paid report in month one.

title: Universal Insurance Claims Rails for Vet Front Desks
one_liner: Vet front desks lose hours filing claims in a dozen insurer portals; sell them one submission and status layer, then add pre-approval and instant-pay as insurers plug in.
customer: Independent clinics and small groups (1-20 locations) with 15-30% insured patients. Later, insurers as per-claim payers.
problem: There are about 6.98M insured animals (+9% in 2025), each insurer has its own portal, forms and record requests, and only 48.2% of practices proactively recommend insurance. Owners often front the full bill. Insurers cannot see clinics, so they lack pre-authorization, real-time pricing and fraud tools.
solution: A browser agent inside the PIMS invoice screen, later API-connected, sends invoice plus records to the right insurer by policy number, tracks status, chases missing documents and reconciles payments. Once volume gives risk data, offer a direct-pay advance so the owner only pays the deductible at checkout.
why_now: Insured animals keep growing while premiums outpace enrollment, so insurers want lower cost-to-adjudicate. Computer-use LLM agents can operate portals without waiting for API deals. Ambient scribes are producing more structured records for claims.
revenue_model: $99-199 per clinic per month, $1-3 per clean claim from insurers later, and a 2-3% fee on advanced claims.
non_obvious_insight: Insurance penetration is partly a back-office problem: the clinic is the distribution channel and is punished with admin work for recommending coverage. Remove the penalty and the recommendation rate rises. The clearinghouse owns the claims data insurers currently cannot see.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 clinics through cloud-PIMS user groups. Shadow the front desk for a week and automate the top 5 insurers by portal. Offer 30 days free, then $99 per month. Measure hours saved per week and days-to-payment.

title: Task-Shifting Engine for Tech-Led Vet Visits
one_liner: Standing-order templates, scheduling and a state-by-state supervision rules database that let clinics move routine care from vets to technicians and, soon, VPAs, without breaking practice acts.
customer: Independent clinics adopting a team-based model, multi-state clinic groups, and VPA-employing practices. Later: PIMS and telehealth vendors licensing the rules API.
problem: Vet supply is nearly flat (91,100 vets; about 3,100 openings a year) while techs are scarce (about 2 per vet versus a 4:1 ideal, with most leaving within 4 years). The team-based model is how affordable clinics reach invoices about 44% below average, yet PIMS scheduling is built around doctor visits. Nobody supplies compliant protocols for who may do what under which supervision in each state.
solution: A library of 'tech appointment' types (booster vaccines, rechecks, suture removal, senior lab draws, weight programs, dental prep) with standing orders, consent scripts and a DVM sign-off queue. A versioned rules database maps each task to state supervision levels, with alerts when boards change rules, and audit logs show who did what under whose supervision. A scheduling plug-in books the right role and length.
why_now: Colorado State is launching an MS for the new VPA license (dogs and cats, supervised, routine surgery and tests), and it has been more than a decade in the making. Roll-ups now span many states, and clinics need to raise output per DVM. AI scribes and agents are generating plans that implicitly delegate tasks.
revenue_model: $199-399 per clinic per month for templates and scheduling; $500-5K per month for rules API and multi-state groups; VPA program design consulting.
non_obvious_insight: A new professional tier shifts value to whoever holds the rules and the protocols. In human health, scope-of-practice changes (NPs, PAs) spawned decades of compliance and protocol software. Vet medicine is at the start of that curve, and the rules database is the moat while templates are the wedge.
first_30_days: With a vet-law attorney, build a matrix of 10 states by about 40 tasks from statutes and board rules. Publish a free 'Can my tech do this?' checker in vet-tech communities. Pilot the appointment templates in 5 clinics and aim to sell 3 multi-state groups on the rules feed.

title: Marginalia: Lived-Experience Annotated Books
one_liner: One-of-one physical books annotated in ink by people who have actually lived what the book is about, such as a retired ER nurse in The Plague or a lighthouse keeper's daughter in To the Lighthouse.
customer: Gift buyers and collectors paying $250-1,200 per copy, quarterly-subscription readers ($180/quarter), independent bookstores, libraries and special collections, and professional associations gifting to retirees.
problem: Explanations and summaries are free and infinite, so 'I've read it' signals nothing. Celebrity-signed copies signal fame, not thought. What is scarce is a particular lived mind reading a text in real time: dated, physical, opinionated, and accountable.
solution: Recruit about 100 'readers of record': retired judges, surgeons, sommeliers, deep-sea divers, and translators. Match each to a canonical book that fits their life. Each annotates a physical copy under a fixed protocol: at least 60 marginal notes, a two-page flyleaf letter, a signed colophon, and a one-take authenticity video. Copies are numbered and sold. A commission tier lets you order a book annotated by someone in your recipient's own profession (a retirement gift for a fire chief). Displaced translators can annotate a translation against the original, showing what the machine misses.
why_now: AI summarizers have made shallow reading free, so deep, lived reading is the differentiator. The 2026 human-made premium is well documented. Physical-book culture is holding up, and the 'association copy' idea is old and understood among collectors.
revenue_model: Per-copy sales (reader 40%, platform about 45%, materials about 15%), a quarterly subscription, institutional acquisitions, and annual charity auctions of 'famous minds' copies.
non_obvious_insight: In an age of infinite explanation, the scarce good is witnessed subjectivity. A marginal note is a physical, un-averaged opinion, the opposite of what a language model produces. Collectors already pay premiums for association copies (a book owned or annotated by someone notable). This manufactures them prospectively and at scale.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 readers through retirement communities and professional associations. Produce 30 copies. Sell through a Substack with page photos and pre-orders. Approach 5 indie bookstores for consignment. Goal: $10k in pre-orders by day 60.

title: Do-Not-Transact Registry: GAMSTOP for Scams
one_liner: An opt-in registry, controlled by consumers and their families, that crypto ATMs, gift-card sellers and wire desks must check before completing a high-risk transaction.
customer: Crypto-ATM operators and gift-card retailers (paying per check and for legal cover). People enroll for free through credit unions, senior centers and adult children.
problem: Crypto-ATM fraud losses rose 58% to $389M in 2025, 66% of it from victims aged 60+. Older adults lost $7.7B overall. Education campaigns fail because scammers coach victims mid-scam to bypass warnings. State AGs have sued major kiosk operators, and cities are considering bans.
solution: People (or a family member with their consent) register commitments made while calm: no cash-to-crypto, no gift cards above $X, no new-payee wires above $Y, bound to ID number and phone. Kiosks that already scan IDs, and retailers via API at gift-card purchase, check the registry and show a neutral refusal script. Lifting a block takes a 72-hour cooling-off period, which breaks the scammer's urgency.
why_now: State kiosk laws (daily caps, mandatory warnings, refunds) and AG lawsuits give operators an urgent need to prove diligence. IC3's 2025 data quantified the elder-loss concentration. Operators may soon need a defensible control to keep their licenses.
revenue_model: About $0.05-0.25 per check plus $500-2K per month per operator. Gift-card processors and retail chains by contract. Grants and credit-union sponsorships fund enrollment.
non_obvious_insight: UK self-exclusion for gambling works because people commit in a calm moment. Scam prevention has assumed you can persuade people mid-scam, which fails. A registry turns consumer protection into a B2B compliance lookup that operators buy for legal cover, so the payer is not the person at risk.
first_30_days: Build an enrollment page and a kiosk-check API. Pilot with one independent operator (100-500 kiosks) and one state credit-union league, and enroll the first 1,000 people through a credit union or senior center. Use the results to brief state legislators and the AG's office.

title: Plug-In Electrification Kits for Landlords
one_liner: Sell curated no-new-circuit kits (120V heat pump water heaters, window heat pumps, induction, balcony solar) to small landlords and housing authorities as an electrician-light retrofit.
customer: Small landlords (1-50 units), property managers and public housing authorities. Utilities and state HEAR programs co-fund the kits.
problem: Data centers pay electricians 25-30% more, so residential contractors cannot staff jobs. Panel upgrades cost $1,500-5,000. Renters and multifamily have no obvious product, and landlords have no reason to pay for tenants' savings.
solution: A packaged program with approved plug-in devices only (UL 3700 balcony solar in states that legalized it, 120V heat pump water heaters, window heat pumps). Maintenance staff or a handyman installs them. The company handles rebate stacking, a lease addendum and tenant paperwork, an insurance rider, and remote monitoring. It also sells a landlord 'plug-in policy in a box' for HOAs and condo boards.
why_now: Nine states had signed plug-in solar laws by September 2026 and UL 3700 now exists. 120V heat pump water heaters and window heat pumps arrived, and housing-authority window heat pump rollouts show large buyers exist. Labor scarcity makes no-electrician products the path of least resistance.
revenue_model: 15-25% gross margin on $1.5-4k kits, a per-unit administration fee from utility and state programs, and SaaS for portfolio managers.
non_obvious_insight: The electrician shortage is the binding constraint, so design products that do not need one. Renter electrification will run through plug-ins, and whoever writes the landlord's compliance and insurance paperwork controls distribution.
first_30_days: Pick two plug-in-friendly states. Assemble a three-SKU kit from existing vendors. Pitch 20 small landlord associations and two housing authorities. Sell 20 kits. Get an insurer's written OK on the rider language.

title: Vape Amnesty: Hazmat Pickup Funds Teen Quitting
angle: Pairing 1: Healthcare/consumer health x Waste/battery recycling
one_liner: Turn the disposable vape from a fire-prone hazmat problem into the top of a cessation funnel: collect vapes at schools and clinics, send the lithium cells to domestic black-mass buyers, and enroll every person who drops one off in a paid quit program.
customer: School districts and county health departments (using youth-vaping settlement and tobacco-prevention funds), plus health plans, Medicaid programs and state quitlines that pay per enrolled quit attempt. Haulers, MRFs and their insurers are a secondary payer for fire-risk reduction.
problem: Vapes are a named driver of the 2026 battery-fire surge: 74 catastrophic facility fires (over $400K each) year to date versus 71 in all of 2024, and one UK hauler saw about 480,000 vapes in two months. Schools confiscate them by the bucket and either pay for hazmat pickup or bin them (nicotine e-liquid can classify as acute hazardous waste in many states, and the cells are Li-ion). Meanwhile cessation programs cannot find teen and young-adult vapers, who do not self-identify.
solution: A 'drop, quit, ship' kit. Fire-rated locking drop boxes sit in school nurse offices, pharmacies, urgent cares and campus clinics. Each box has a QR code that opens a confidential text-based quit coach, with a telehealth clinician for pharmacotherapy where the user is old enough. A licensed universal-waste hauler batches the vapes, discharges and extracts the cells for black-mass sale, and manifests the e-liquid. Districts get a compliance report and an 'alternative to suspension' curriculum. Public health gets anonymized data on which illicit brands and flavors are turning up.
why_now: The Aug 27, 2026 BIS rule forces black mass to be sold to US buyers, so recovered cells have a guaranteed domestic outlet. Battery-fire counts are at 10-year highs and nobody has decided who pays for the losses. California just expanded battery EPR (SB 501). Youth-vaping settlement money is still being allocated by states and districts.
revenue_model: Per-school or per-clinic annual fee for boxes, pickups and compliance reporting ($1-3K per site). A bounty per enrolled quit attempt from plans and state programs. A small hauler and insurer sponsorship for avoided fire exposure. Black-mass proceeds are trivial (a tonne is roughly 50-100K vapes), so the business runs on the public-health and hazmat budgets, not on the materials.
non_obvious_insight: Two budgets that never talk to each other, public health (which pays for quits but cannot find the user) and waste operations (which finds the user's object but only sees a hazard), both pay to touch the same physical item. A vape in a drop box is a self-identified nicotine-dependent person at peak motivation.
first_30_days: Pitch 3 school districts and 1 county health department on a free 'amnesty week' at two high schools. Buy 10 fire-rated collection containers and sign a licensed universal-waste hauler. White-label an existing text-quit vendor. Collect the first ~200 vapes, count flavors and brands, and publish a one-page fire-risk and quit-enrollment report to convert the pilots into paid annual contracts.

title: Blue Tarp Index: Adjuster Ground Truth for ILS
one_liner: A subscription that sells cat-bond and reinsurance investors what veteran field adjusters can see in the first 10 days after a disaster, before any model or carrier report exists.
customer: ILS funds, cat bond trading desks, reinsurance-broker analytics teams, and hedge-fund or equity analysts covering Florida, Gulf and California-exposed carriers. Roughly $30k-$120k per year per team.
problem: Post-event loss estimates swing wildly (Milton was pegged anywhere from a few tens of billions up, and cat-bond implied-loss marks moved daily) and settle slowly. The cat bond market is now about $65.6B outstanding after a record $17.6B of H1 2026 issuance, and most of that capital marks to modeler guesses and carrier press releases. Investors have no structured ground truth for the variables that decide severity: how many roofs really failed, whether demand surge is 10% or 40%, and whether contractors can staff repairs at all.
solution: A vetted panel of 60-150 independent veteran cat adjusters files 10-minute standardized mobile observations on publicly visible conditions only: blue-tarp density per 100 roofs on sampled blocks, roofing debris and dumpster counts, mystery-shopped contractor and tarp-crew quotes ($/sq, lead times), hotel and RV occupancy, and adjuster deployment density. Outputs are an event dashboard, a 'Blue Tarp Index' and a demand-surge index within 72 hours to 10 days, a weekly note, and paid expert calls. Hard rule, reviewed by counsel: no claim-file, policyholder or carrier-confidential information, only public observation and market pricing, aggregated and anonymized.
why_now: Cat bond and ILS capital hit records in 2026, with over $120B of ILS capacity, so more money is exposed to event-loss uncertainty than ever. Claims-adjuster employment fell about 21% year over year through May 2026 as carriers automate, which leaves a large pool of experienced people who need income and are cheap to recruit. The very quiet 2026 Atlantic season (no hurricane until at least Sept 11) gives a scrappy team time to build and back-test before the next event. Wildfire, hail and flood events also count as live tests.
revenue_model: Annual subscription tiers ($25k signal-only, $60k with expert calls, $120k+ bespoke event coverage), per-event pay-per-call expert sessions, and paid retrospective studies. Adjusters get $75-$150 per completed field report plus a revenue share pool. Gross margin is high because the data is field labor, not infrastructure.
non_obvious_insight: Models price wind and exposure, but severity in the real world is set by contractor capacity: how many roofers, tarp crews and drying crews physically exist within 200 miles. An adjuster feels that constraint on day 4 because they cannot get a tarp crew to a house, and nobody in finance measures it. Tarps are also what the policy pays for first, so their density is a fast, visible proxy for claim frequency. The hypothesis is testable by back-testing against Helene, Milton and the LA fires.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 laid-off or semi-retired cat adjusters from cat-adjuster Facebook groups, adjuster forums and LinkedIn. Draft the observation protocol and a counsel-approved compliance memo. Run a retrospective 'what we would have told you on day 7' study on Helene/Milton and the Jan 2025 LA fires using panel memory, public imagery and contractor pricing archives. Publish a free sample note, send it to 15 ILS portfolio managers and 5 broker analytics heads, and aim for 2-3 paid pilots ($15-25k) that include the retro study as a deliverable, with the first live test on spring 2027 hail or a wildfire.

title: Personalized Cancer Vaccines for Dogs
one_liner: Falling costs of tumor sequencing, neoantigen prediction and small-batch mRNA make a bespoke cancer vaccine per dog plausible; start with the sequencing and design report oncologists can order today.
customer: Veterinary oncologists and university teaching hospitals, and owners of dogs with newly diagnosed aggressive cancers (hemangiosarcoma, osteosarcoma, mast cell tumors, lymphoma).
problem: Owners of dogs with cancer are offered chemo, surgery or nothing. The briefing notes about 80% of dogs with lymphoma never get IV chemo, and only one oral option has recently arrived. Owners will pay for hope, but experimental individualized therapies are inaccessible, and existing genomic panels mainly match small-molecule drugs rather than designing a vaccine.
solution: Phase 1: tumor-normal sequencing, neoantigen ranking and a clinician report in about 10 days, sold to oncologists. Phase 2: under a vet-school client-owned-dog research protocol, produce an individualized mRNA vaccine through a small-batch CDMO, with regulatory strategy set with USDA veterinary biologics and FDA CVM.
why_now: Sequencing runs at a few hundred dollars per genome, open protein and neoantigen prediction tools are strong, small-batch mRNA manufacturing is contract-accessible, and human personalized-vaccine programs are running. Loyal's conditional-approval progress shows vet regulators will work with novel therapies.
revenue_model: $1.5-3K per sequencing report, $10-25K per vaccine research-protocol fee, and licensing of the genomic dataset to human-oncology developers.
non_obvious_insight: Dogs are an excellent human-cancer model: spontaneous tumors, shorter timelines, owner-funded and lighter regulatory burden than humans. The paid 'hope' market is outside insurance, and the tumor-normal dataset itself is a licensable asset.
first_30_days: Partner with one vet-school oncology service and a sequencing lab. Enroll the first 10 dogs for sequencing-only analysis at cost. Sign an MOU with a small-batch mRNA CDMO. Submit a research protocol and recruit through oncologist referrals and owner communities. Individualized therapy remains experimental, so set expectations accordingly.

title: Texas Data-Center Water Filing and Attestation
one_liner: A fixed-fee compliance service that meters, calculates, files and PE-attests data-center water reports for the operators who ignored Texas's mandatory water survey.
customer: About 280 non-responding Texas data centers (colos, crypto miners, enterprise sites, edge facilities) and developers of the roughly 1,800 projects held in the ERCOT queue. The operator or developer pays.
problem: Only 17% of 341 surveyed Texas data centers answered the mandatory 2025 water survey (maximum fine $500). On Aug 3 the governor froze ERCOT connection approvals pending a water and energy audit, and TWDB owes an update by Oct 14, 2026. Non-reporting is about to become a crime and a bar to TCEQ permits and interconnection. Small operators have no in-house water or regulatory staff.
solution: A turnkey filing: interpret the survey, verify or install non-invasive clamp-on flow metering on make-up and blowdown lines, reconcile utility bills, compute WUE plus scarcity-adjusted and grid-indirect water, then have a Texas licensed PE sign an attestation. Keep an audit-ready data room and issue quarterly updates as rules change.
why_now: The freeze, the Oct 14 update and the coming criminal penalties all land within weeks. A stamp from an independent PE unblocks permits and interconnection, and nobody else sells it to the long tail.
revenue_model: $5-15k per-facility filing package, $2-5k/month recurring attestation, $50-200k portfolio deals. Anonymized data becomes the first scarcity-adjusted benchmark set.
non_obvious_insight: The hyperscalers will self-certify. The 83% who did not respond, mostly small and mid-size operators, will be the first enforcement targets. Enforcement demand arrives suddenly, and whoever has met 50 operators and installed 50 meters in the first wave owns the reference dataset.
first_30_days: Build a list of Texas data centers from public survey and ERCOT queue records. Partner with a Texas engineering firm for PE stamps. Host a 'what to do before Oct 14' webinar, cold-email 100 non-responders, and close the first five filings at $5-10k.

title: Test-once PFAS proof registry for packaging importers
one_liner: A SKU-level registry and group-buy of accredited PFAS lab reports, so importers of the same factory's food packaging share one test and can produce an authority-ready dossier fast.
customer: EU importers, wholesalers and white-label brands of grease-resistant paper and fibre food packaging (takeaway boxes, bakery bags, burger wraps, pizza boxes, cups), plus online B2B packaging shops. Owners, purchasing or QA managers pay.
problem: Since 12 Aug 2026 the packaging regulation bans PFAS in food-contact packaging above limits (25 ppb per non-polymeric substance, 250 ppb sum, 50 ppm total PFAS), with no grandfathering for stock made earlier. Compliance guides say supplier self-declarations are not proof and that importers and producers carry the liability, with accredited-lab reports needed per packaging type. Authorities can request the technical documentation on short notice. There is no harmonised EU test method and lab capacity is finite. Each importer paying separately for the same factory's product is wasteful.
solution: A registry keyed to product specification, coating, factory and production lot. Factories, labs and importers upload accredited lab reports (cheap total organic fluorine screening first, then targeted LC-MS/MS). Other importers of the same factory and spec can match and attach the report to their own technical file. A lot-matching check and re-test reminders keep the proof valid, and an 'authority request pack' export assembles the file in one click. Group-buy: when several importers sell the same SKU, the platform pools the cost of one accredited test and negotiates volume prices with 2-3 labs. Each importer remains legally responsible, so the tool shows exactly what evidence it does and does not cover.
why_now: The ban applied on 12 Aug 2026, six weeks ago, and stock made before then cannot be sold. Labs expect demand to climb through enforcement and there is no harmonised method yet, so evidence quality varies.
revenue_model: EUR 150-400 per verified report access, EUR 25 per month per SKU for monitoring and re-test alerts, plus a 10-15% margin on group-purchased lab tests. Optional paid dossier assembly at EUR 300-600.
non_obvious_insight: Every importer treats PFAS proof as its own cost, but the object being proven is the packaging type. The same few hundred factory SKUs flow through thousands of importers, which creates network effects for a 'test once, verify per lot' registry that no consultancy or lab has an incentive to build. Evidence: guides state that 'self-declarations from suppliers do not constitute proof' and that certificates of analysis are needed per packaging type (https://www.certivo.com/blog-details/ppwr-pfas-ban-in-food-contact-packaging-what-manufacturers-must-have-ready-by-august-2026); the ban has no grandfather clause and responsibility falls on manufacturers and importers (https://www.kivo.nl/en/knowledge-base/pfas-ban-in-food-packaging-what-does-it-mean-for-your-products/); testing runs from a few hundred euros for screening to several thousand for targeted analysis, labs have limited capacity, and no harmonised EU method exists (https://pakfactory.com/blog/how-to-test-packaging-for-pfas; https://foodpackagingforum.org/news/ppwr-pfas-limits-apply-from-august-12).
first_30_days: Sign volume pricing with 2 accredited labs for TOF screening and targeted panels. Recruit 10 importers from packaging trade associations, LinkedIn groups and B2B packaging marketplaces. Ask them to list their top 20 SKUs and factories, then find overlaps between them. Run the first pooled test for the most-shared SKU at a per-importer cost far below a solo test. Publish a free 'PFAS status per SKU' lookup to attract more importers. Legal-review the shared-report disclaimer language with a food-contact lawyer.

title: Evac Cash: Payout When Ordered to Evacuate
one_liner: A few dollars a month buys a $500-$2,500 wire within hours of an official mandatory evacuation order for your address, covering hurricane, wildfire and burn-scar flood orders.
customer: Renters and lower-to-middle-income homeowners in evacuation zones: Gulf and Florida surge zones, Western wildfire-urban-interface neighborhoods, and LA burn-scar areas. Sold to individuals, through employers of hourly staff (hospitals, hotels, nursing homes, grocers), and through credit unions or municipal 'evac funds'.
problem: Evacuating costs $1,000-$3,000 (gas, hotel, lost shifts, pet boarding) and the money is needed before any claim exists. Cost is a common reason people stay, so the people most exposed are least able to leave. Civil-authority and additional-living-expense cover is slow, receipt-based, often conditional on nearby damage, and many renters lack it.
solution: A parametric contract whose trigger is a legal act. If your geocoded address sits inside a polygon under a mandatory evacuation order, or an NWS flash-flood emergency for a burn scar, the platform pays via FedNow/RTP or a push-to-card within hours. Zone data comes from county emergency-management systems (evacuation-zone platforms and state zone maps). Tiers are priced by zone frequency, with one payout per event per address and a simple app that alerts you and shows your zone. Underwritten via a licensed MGA and fronting carrier, first as employer group policies.
why_now: Address-level, machine-readable evacuation zones are now common. FedNow/RTP make hours-not-weeks payouts cheap. The LA fires of January 2025 made burn-scar exposure vivid, and NOAA CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks show a greater than 90% chance of a very strong El Niño this winter, which means heavy rain on fresh burn scars and flash-flood/debris-flow evacuation orders. Parametric reinsurance capacity is plentiful and MGAs want small-ticket distribution.
revenue_model: Premium of roughly $3-$15 per month depending on how often each zone is ordered out (about 1.3-1.5x expected payout), or $1-$3 per employee per month on group plans. The company keeps an MGA commission of 15-25%, plus municipal, nonprofit and employer-funded policies for vulnerable residents. Later it can sell zone-frequency data to emergency managers.
non_obvious_insight: The best parametric trigger is a legal act, not a physical measurement. An evacuation order is binary, public, address-specific and timestamped, so basis risk nearly vanishes. Paying people to leave also changes behavior and saves lives, which makes employers and governments willing co-payers, so the product has two buyers instead of one.
first_30_days: Sign a parametric MGA and fronting carrier. Build the polygon match and instant-payout flow on public evacuation-zone data. Pilot a group policy for about 200 hourly workers at one Gulf hospital or hotel employer and one credit union serving a LA burn-scar community. Offer emergency-management agencies a free 'what zone am I in' tool for distribution. Goal: 500 covered addresses before peak rain season.

title: Aid-in-Dying Program-in-a-Box for Hospices
one_liner: Sell newly-legal states' hospices and health systems the policies, forms, trained consulting-clinician panel and logistics they need to participate in medical aid in dying.
customer: Independent hospices, palliative practices and non-religious health systems in Illinois and New York, then Massachusetts and Pennsylvania if they pass. The buyer is the medical director or administrator.
problem: Legalization creates a right on paper. The bottleneck is willing, trained clinicians (attending plus consulting physician, and mental-health evaluation where required), statutory documentation, waiting periods, pharmacy sourcing and staff opt-out policies. Most providers have no playbook, so patients bounce between systems that opt out. Advocacy groups cover navigation, not staffing.
solution: A turnkey program: policy templates, staff training, state-specific e-documentation workflows, an on-call roster of trained consulting physicians and evaluators (licensed per state, telehealth where allowed), pharmacy coordination, family support, and post-death reporting. The service serves only patient-initiated requests and supports providers that opt in.
why_now: New York's law was signed Feb 6, 2026, and Illinois's law, signed Dec 12, 2025, takes effect this month (Sept 2026). Two large states are opening within months, with 14 jurisdictions now having some form of law and more pending. Scheduled deaths also create planning lead time that sudden deaths never had.
revenue_model: $15-40K program onboarding fee, $500-$1,000 per consult or evaluation, and per-case coordination fees. State grants are possible.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is not legal permission but willing clinicians and paperwork bandwidth, so the money is in clinical capacity and compliance, which advocacy nonprofits don't provide.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 physicians with prior Oregon or Washington experience as advisors. Approach 10 independent Illinois hospices. Sell a $7.5K readiness assessment plus policy pack first. Start recruiting a consulting-physician roster and get counsel to confirm state rules on telehealth and referral fees.

title: School Deepfake-Nude Incident Response Retainer
one_liner: A 24/7 retainer that walks school districts through the first 72 hours of an AI-generated nude incident: hash-based takedowns, evidence handling, reporting duties and parent communications.
customer: School districts, charter networks and independent schools. Channel: school risk pools, cyber and liability insurers and brokers.
problem: Nudify apps let anyone turn a student photo into sexual imagery. Schools improvise: staff viewing the images can itself be illegal, mandated-reporting and Title IX duties are unclear, and takedowns must be filed on many platforms. The federal TAKE IT DOWN Act (2025) requires platforms to remove reported intimate imagery within 48 hours, with platform compliance due May 2026 (from memory), but victims and schools don't know the process.
solution: A playbook plus tooling: secure intake that hashes images without staff viewing them (StopNCII and NCMEC Take It Down style), pre-filled takedown requests, a state-by-state legal duty checklist, evidence logs, communication templates for parents and students, and counselor referral. A retained hotline handles live incidents.
why_now: The TAKE IT DOWN Act's platform obligations kicked in this year, incidents are proliferating, and insurers are re-underwriting districts for cyber and child-safety exposure.
revenue_model: $3-12k annual retainer per district, per-incident fees, and bundle or referral deals with insurers and school risk pools.
non_obvious_insight: The worst thing a school can do is look at the evidence, so the product is a don't-look-just-hash workflow. Insurers are the channel because one mishandled incident costs far more than the retainer.
first_30_days: Draft the playbook with a school-law attorney and a former juvenile detective. Pitch 3 school-insurance brokers or state school-board risk pools. Run free tabletop exercises for 5 districts. Convert the best relationship into the first paid retainer.

title: Paid Neighbor Walking Routes for Absent Kids
one_liner: Hire retired neighbors and parents as paid 'route captains' who walk or wake up chronically absent kids on fixed blocks, and get paid a share of the funding that the recovered attendance brings back.
customer: Principals and districts in states that fund schools on average daily attendance (California, Texas and similar). Secondary payers are city safe-passage budgets, Title I funds and Medicaid plans (for asthma and chronic-condition kids).
problem: About one in four kids is chronically absent. Nudge letters and text campaigns work on the 10 to 19 day group but barely touch the kids missing 25 or more days. For them it is a 7:40 a.m. logistics problem: a parent working an early shift, an older sibling who moved on to middle school, a dangerous corner, no clean clothes, no alarm clock. In attendance-funded states, each absent day costs the school roughly what a day of instruction is worth, so a $200-per-kid fix pays back several times over.
solution: Micro-employ 3 to 5 route captains per school as part-time W-2 workers (7:00 to 8:30 a.m., roughly $18 an hour). Each captain covers a block-by-block route, walking 6 to 10 kids, knocking on doors, and running a breakfast and laundry pass. Captains report barrier codes by voice note, which feed the attendance team's dashboard. Contract as a base route fee plus 20 to 25 percent of documented funding gains from improved attendance.
why_now: Chronic absenteeism has not returned to pre-pandemic levels. ESSER-funded attendance staff were cut as that money expired. States now require chronic-absence plans, and the retiree and gig-worker labor pool is looking for short, local, part-time work.
revenue_model: Base fee per route plus a performance share of recovered attendance funding. Optional per-route sponsorship from health plans or employers.
non_obvious_insight: Districts spend on software and letters, but the students who cost the most are the ones for whom the 7:40 a.m. logistics fail. The cheapest fix is a grandmother on the corner, and it is invisible to edtech buyers because it is not a product. The first three Mondays of September predict the year, so contracting has to start before October.
first_30_days: Pilot with one principal in an attendance-funded state: 2 routes, about 12 kids, 4 part-time captains recruited from churches and senior centers. Establish baselines from last year's attendance data and track days present weekly. Write the performance addendum as a one-page contract that a principal can sign with discretionary funds and later convert to a district contract.

title: Hotel-Signed Days-in-Country Proofs for Remote Teams
one_liner: Hotels and co-living spaces issue signed, privacy-minimal 'nights in this country' attestations, so employers can prove where remote staff worked without tracking their phones.
customer: Finance, tax or mobility leads at remote-first companies of 30-500 staff that run 'work from anywhere' weeks. Secondary payers are co-living operators and boutique hotels that want a 'workation-verified' badge.
problem: A few weeks abroad can create payroll, social-security and permanent-establishment exposure, and employers need day counts to defend their position. In the EU, GPS or phone tracking of staff is legally toxic (GDPR proportionality, works councils), so companies rely on self-reported spreadsheets. The EU Entry/Exit System has logged border crossings automatically since April 2026, yet neither traveler nor employer gets that data in a usable form. 40+ nomad-visa regimes each have different thresholds.
solution: A thin layer on top of hotel and co-living check-in. At checkout the guest opts in, and the property issues a signed attestation (country, region, date range, licence ID, guest name and nothing else) into the traveler's wallet. The employer's HR or tax tool ingests it by CSV or API, and a country rules pack warns when a threshold is near. The MVP needs no integration: a web form, a signed PDF with a QR code, and a shared ledger template.
why_now: EES has been fully live since 10 Apr 2026, so stays are now machine-tracked at the border but invisible to employers. ETIAS slipping to 2027 keeps the friction alive. Hybrid and workation policies have matured, and 40+ nomad visas make cross-border patchwork the norm.
revenue_model: The employer pays about $6 per attestation or $10 per employee per year for the ledger and rules pack. The property pays about $49 a month for a verified listing in a 'workation-ready' directory. Tax advisers can resell it.
non_obvious_insight: Employers cannot lawfully surveil location, but hospitality already produces third-party presence records by law (guest registration and folios). The missing piece is a consent-based export, so the evidence sits in the hotel and not on the phone.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 co-living spaces and boutique hotels (Lisbon, Canaries, Split, Tbilisi) through operator communities. Have one cross-border tax adviser review a one-page attestation spec. Issue attestations by hand. Pitch 5 remote-first startups through their payroll and tax advisers at a $500 pilot, and count first revenue when the first ledger is delivered.
